title: Home of Forgotten Memories
subtitle: The dead are not truly gone so long as they are remembered.

items.text: A flash of light materializes in empty space, sending three figures tumbling into a vast golden plain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: *panting* We should be safe out here.
Mesmer Jr. glances back. There's no one behind them.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Was that an earthquake?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. There's something big coming from the exhibition hall.
A massive robot with long, wiry arms and a spherical head appears. It pauses in place and begins surveying the surroundings.
Its head rotates in a full circle as it completes a thorough scan.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: What is that?!
The massive robot seems to lock onto them from afar and starts bounding toward them at incredible speed.

items.speaker: X
items.text: *sigh* Looks like things are about to get even more dangerous.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But hey, good news: there's a building over there.
X points to the distance, where an old apartment building juts out from the golden fields.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's take shelter there.
They crouch down in tall wheat and scurry toward the building.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Quick, get down!
The apartment appears to be abandoned. The back gate is weathered and worn, and the surrounding wall is overgrown with vines.
The three hurry over to the doorway. As the giant robot's footsteps grow louder and louder, they slip inside the building.
They press their ears against the door to listen to the sounds outside.
Boom!!
Boom!
The sounds beyond the door fade. The giant robot seems to have passed by them, but the three of them are still holding stiff, barely breathing.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I think it's gone for now.
The tension finally eases. The three slump to the ground, leaning against the door.

items.speaker: X
items.text: *sigh* Isn't sending such a super-sized robot after us a little extreme?
X waves his hands and starts looking around their hiding place.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hah. Neat interior, smells lived-in, traces of mold removal on the walls ...
Gaining a bit of resolve, they begin to explore the empty building.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But where are the residents?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This place feels strange. It's almost like ...
X opens a red refrigerator. Thankfully, there are no metal tendrils inside, only packaged food—unopened tins of cookies, bags of sugar, unused butter ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: No sign of any robotic technology in here, and all the food is untouched. It's like this house has been isolated from the outside world for years. And yet ...
The young visitor looks around, taking stock of the items strewn about the house.

items.speaker: X
items.text: A plow, three oil pastels ... and an assortment of strange alarm clocks, a few syringes, and a bottle of men's cologne?

items.speaker: X
items.text: These things don't look like they belong to a family, but rather a dozen people or so, with their lives all mixed together.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's some personal effects in here: letters, family photos, and ...

items.speaker: Chirper
items.text: "I've started recording. C'mon, Mama!"

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: What's that sound?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's coming from this pocket watch device. That journalist we met, Maxim, he had something like this too.

items.speaker: Chirper
items.text: "Don't worry. I'm recovering well here. All of us comrades in the ward do what we can to help each other, so we can overcome any difficulties."

items.speaker: Chirper
items.text: "Don't forget about me, Mama! I really miss you, Papa. It's already been a month."

items.speaker: Chirper
items.text: "I remember, little squirrel. The next time you visit, remember to bring that doll with you, the one with the pretty floral dress, on the balcony."
The pocket watch falls silent.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Were they the owners of this apartment? Where did they go?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not a clue.
There's all sorts of things on the balcony, but the doll isn't here.
From behind them, they hear the sound of a gun being cocked. X is about to turn when a shout stops him in his tracks.
Don't move! Put your hands up first, then turn around slowly.
They carefully raise their arms and turn to face the person behind them. A tense old woman is brandishing a shotgun.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please don't shoot, ma'am. We're just ...
Call me Tamara.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Foreign kids, a rare sight. The last time I saw misbehaving kids was before the Plague. It's a shame so many lives were cut short.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: What'd you do to anger a Belyash like that? Steal its H-beams?
The old woman examines the three of them closely.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Oh, I see. You're those unknown variables Zina was talking about.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Alright, tell me what happened. Don't they tell you to obey your elders where you're from?
The young intruders look at each other in stunned silence. Finally, X steps forward.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Allow me to explain, Madam Tamara.

items.speaker: X
items.text: And that's what happened, ma'am. I swear everything we've said is the truth.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Just another group of foolish kids caught up in a conflict they shouldn't have been a part of—if I take you at your word, that is.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: But branding three kids terrorists and sending out a Belyash to stop them? The people in this country have gone mad!

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You have my sympathy, anyway. But I have more important things to do than babysit.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Considering your situation, how about you hide here a little longer? When I'm done with my work, I can send someone to help you out with the orb-head outside.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: But all this is a memorial for the good folks we'd lost to the Plague, so don't touch anything.
The three exchange glances.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Or you can always leave. God knows I won't stop you.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: We'll accept your offer, ma'am.
X cuts in before Mesmer Jr. can finish her sentence. He shoots her a sidelong glance, as if pleading for her to follow his lead.
Mesmer follows his gaze to the shotgun in Madam Tamara's hands.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Not like we can confront the Belyash with just the three of us. Might as well stay put for now, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It does make sense.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll stay and help you, Madam Tamara.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Then you're smarter than I took you for. Relax, I won't hurt you. Come, look.
*ring*
An alarm clock starts ringing. Tamara turns to the assorted collection of clocks in the room and quickly singles out the source.
She approaches the old clock and shuts it off with a sigh.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: *sigh* I think of this place as a memorial. Although it doesn't commemorate any heroes, just everyday people, like the one who owned all these clocks.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: They belonged to Olga Sokolova, a 23-year-old nurse. A very jumpy, anxious girl, but honest. Taking care of her possessions takes a lot of effort.
*ring* Another alarm clock starts ringing from somewhere in the room.

items.speaker: Alarm Clock
items.text: "Patient No. 28 needs their medication!"
Tamara's hand weaves through the forest of alarm clocks on the windowsill with ease and shuts off the rattling timer.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Why did she need so many clocks?

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Ah, Olga was terrified of forgetting all sorts of things. She'd set her alarms to remind her to administer medication, shots ... You get the idea, but it wasn't enough.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: In the end, she went to the hospital too, leaving me with this mess.

items.speaker: X
items.text: This one looks the oldest.
X picks up a children's alarm clock made of old, yellowed plastic.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You're right. That was the first. It'll ring in just a moment. It's why I came here today.
Everyone quiets down, waiting for the little alarm to ring.

items.speaker: Children's Alarm Clock
items.text: "Happy 20th birthday, Sasha."

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: You can turn it off now. Her daughter isn't around to hear it. The Plague took her, just like so many others. 20 years old ... How time flies.
Tamara picks up a broom leaning against the corner of the room.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: *sigh* Kids, come give me a hand.
The young visitors follow Tamara to another corner of the room, one that seems entirely different in style.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: An entire wall of tools. Looks like whoever lived here liked making things by hand.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: That's an understatement. There's a basket under the workbench full of all kinds of toys and electronic parts. Andrey and Vanya loved tinkering with those kinds of things.
Tamara starts sweeping with one hand and pulls a few rags from a nearby plastic bag with the other, handing them out to the young visitors.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Alright, kids, the sooner we finish cleaning, the sooner we can deal with that hunk of metal outside.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Maybe I'll bring a few robots over to show my old friends how much our country has developed.
The three of them each take a rag and approach the wall of tools.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Is this why you've been keeping things just the way they were?
Tamara sweeps up the dust under the bench, then stops to massage her lower back.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: This isn't really their home. I just moved their things here. Like taking a snapshot of their former lives. A cenotaph for the dead.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: I'm old. And the older I get, the more I recall my past memories. Everyone moved on so quickly. I couldn't bear to throw anything away, so I put it all here.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: Zina called it stupid, heh heh. But she didn't stop me, either.
Tamara empties her dustpan. She flips open the calendar hanging from the door.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: At the height of the Plague, none of us would say it, but we all wondered the same thing: Is humanity doomed?

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: But even so, no one gave up. Everyone kept on stubbornly surviving, as if we could outlast the whole disaster, outlast the sun itself, whatever it took to see our lives return to normal.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: We would say, "Who better to withstand the harsh winter than us?" We would help each other, encourage each other through the hard moments. We let the flames of our most fervent hopes warm our hands.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: We kept telling ourselves, "Don't cry. If we sow our seeds today, we'll reap a bountiful harvest in the future."

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: But some never saw the spring.
Mesmer Jr. lowers her head. She keeps on wiping the same spot on the glass cabinet door, even though it's already sparkling clean.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: My condolences.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: *sigh* To be honest, after so many years have passed, even the grief has faded.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: But once in a while, I find myself thinking that the happiness we have today is something they'll never see.
Tamara walks over to the workbench and picks up a picture frame.
In the photo, there's a man in greasy overalls hugging a young boy, who's holding up a robot.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: If Andrey and little Vanya were still alive, they would've been overjoyed to see a world covered in metal machines.

items.speaker: Tamara
items.text: And Vanya's mother, Rozaliya ... She would've been happy too.
Mesmer Jr. looks over at Tamara and sighs.
Her breath fogs up the glass, but Mesmer Jr. moves on and starts wiping up somewhere else.
Tamara sets the picture frame back down.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Hmm. Strange.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What is it?
Mesmer Jr. lifts the picture frame.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We saw this person at the summit.
